主要内容: The article discusses the hidden ties between the 'Friends of the Court' and big investors, highlighting how these legal entities can influence judicial decisions. It focuses on the case involving Bruce Berkowitz, a wealthy Miami investor, and his firm, Fairholme Funds, who are betting on a rebound in the shares of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. These mortgage giants were rescued by the U.S. government during the financial crisis. The article reveals that Cooper & Kirk PLLC, led by Chuck Cooper, submitted a legal brief to support the investors' case, even going as far as hiding their involvement by having another attorney submit it in her name. This practice raises concerns about the transparency of amicus curiae briefs, which are meant to provide outside perspectives to judges. The article also notes that many of the amicus briefs filed in these cases are linked to the investors, with some not disclosing their ties to the judges. The U.S. Supreme Court and federal appeals courts require disclosure of payments for amicus briefs but not other ties, which can allow well-funded litigants to sway judicial outcomes. The article also discusses the legal battle involving Bruce Berkowitz's Fairholme Funds and the U.S. government's handling of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. Berkowitz, a known contrarian investor, invested heavily in the preferred shares of these mortgage giants, which are now nearly a third of his $2.2 billion fund. He argued that the government's actions in 2013, which began pocketing all profits from Fannie and Freddie, violated the Fifth Amendment by taking private property without compensation. Cooper & Kirk, a law firm with ties to Supreme Court Justice William Rehnquist's former clerk, has been representing Berkowitz in court, filing amicus briefs in multiple cases. The firm's legal strategy includes challenging the government's actions in the U.S. Court of Federal Claims. Meanwhile, the case of Anthony 'Buddy' Piszel, a former Freddie Mac CFO, also presents a potential threat to the Fairholme suit, as the court was considering his case last year.
